title: An Enzyme-free Method for Isolation and Expansion of Human Adipose-derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells.
markdown:
## Protocol: I want to recover mesenchymal stromal cells from a human lipoaspirate sample without digesting the starting tissue with collagenase or another dissociation enzyme. Describe how to set up explant outgrowth cultures, collect adherent cells, and passage them for expansion. Enzymatic detachment during later passaging is acceptable.

### Overview

This protocol outlines the isolation of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) from human lipoaspirate or abdominoplasty samples using an explant outgrowth method. This approach avoids enzymatic digestion of the starting tissue with collagenase or other dissociation enzymes. The process involves sample acquisition, aseptic processing, tissue mincing, plating for cell migration, and subsequent expansion of adherent cells via enzymatic detachment during passaging.

### Materials/Reagents

Dulbecco's minimal essential media (DMEM) with high glucose and 2 mM L-glutamine; Defined fetal calf serum (FCS); Penicillin-Streptomycin (10,000 U/100 mL); Trypsin with 0.25% EDTA; 1x Phosphate buffered saline (PBS); 10% Bleach; 70% Ethanol; Sterile PBS (for keeping abdominoplasty samples moist).

### Equipment

Laminar flow hood; Sterile 100 mm vacuum-gas plasma treated tissue culture plates; Conical centrifuge tubes; Hemocytometer; Centrifuge capable of 300 x g; Sterile scalpel; Sterile forceps; Sterile needle; Paper towels.

### Safety & Sterility

Conduct all steps from tissue mincing onwards in a laminar flow hood under aseptic conditions. Wear gloves for personal protection. Keep 10% bleach, 70% ethanol, and paper towels nearby to quickly clean up any biological spills. Dispose of any excess tissue as biomedical waste.

## Reagent Preparation

### Prior to isolating ASCs

1. Sterilely prepare 500 mL of tissue culture media prior to isolating adipose-derived stem cells (ASCs) by adding 10% defined fetal calf serum (FCS) and Penicillin-Streptomycin (10,000 U/100 mL) to Dulbecco's minimal essential media (DMEM) with high glucose and 2 mM L-glutamine. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Store the prepared media at 4 °C for up to 3 weeks and ensure it is used warm (between room temperature to 37 °C) when needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->

#### Branch: Alternative Media

1. If a different media is preferred for the culture of the stem cells, prepare that specific media instead of the standard DMEM formulation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Culture of ASCs

### when the parent plate reaches approximately 70% confluency

> **Operational constraint:** Passage the ASCs when the parent plate reaches approximately 70% confluency, taking care to avoid over-confluency of the cultures. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
1. Gently rinse the plate with 1x phosphate buffered saline, aspirate the saline, add 1 mL of Trypsin with 0.25% EDTA to each plate, and incubate at 37 °C for 5 minutes to trypsinize the adherent cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->

### After 5 min

1. After 5 minutes, confirm de-adherence by microscopy. If the cells are still adherent, return the cells to the incubator for an additional 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->

#### Branch: Cells Still Adherent

1. If the cells are still adherent after the initial check, return the cells to the incubator for an additional 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S02 -->

### Deactivation and Washing

1. Add a small amount of media (approximately 25% of the total trypsin volume) to the plate to deactivate the trypsin. Gently wash the base of the plate by holding it at a slight angle and pipetting the media/trypsin mixture from the top downwards to loosen any weakly attached cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
2. Re-plate the cells at a 1:3 ratio or seed them at a density of 120,000-500,000 cells per plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->

### Seeding based on cell count

#### Branch: Seeding based on cell count

1. If seeding based on cell count, transfer the trypsin/media mixture from the plate into a conical centrifuge tube and pellet the cells by centrifugation at 300 x g for 7 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S01 -->
2. Resuspend the cells in tissue culture media (approximately 1 mL per initial plate) and count them prior to seeding. To count, transfer 10 μL of the cell suspension into a hemocytometer, count the cells in the 4x4 quadrant at each corner of the grid, average these values, and multiply by 10^4 to calculate the cell number. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S02 -->

### Final Seeding

1. Add media to the new plate prior to seeding. Add the cells in a dropwise manner and swirl the plate to ensure even distribution across the surface. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T4-S01 -->

## Isolation of ASCs from Adipose Tissue

### Sample Acquisition and Storage

1. Obtain lipoaspirates or abdominoplasty samples following IRB approval as discard tissue from surgical procedures. Transport lipoaspirates in the vessel used by the surgeon, and transport abdominoplasty samples in an operating room specimen bag or container. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Store the samples at room temperature for up to 6 hours or at 4 °C for up to 24 hours if not processing immediately, as delayed processing may diminish cell yield. Keep abdominoplasty samples moist by adding 1x sterile phosphate buffered saline. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->

### Aseptic Processing Setup

> **Operational constraint:** From this point onwards, conduct all steps in a laminar flow hood under aseptic conditions while wearing gloves. Keep 10% bleach, 70% ethanol, and paper towels nearby for spill cleanup, and dispose of excess tissue as biomedical waste. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Tissue Mincing

1. Mince the samples into pieces smaller than 1 mm. If an abdominoplasty block is too large, cut off a manageable size first. Transfer the tissue to the lid of a sterile 100 mm plate, hold a piece in place with a sterile needle, and use a sterile scalpel to mince the pieces off by cutting or gently shredding them from the bulk tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

#### Branch: Lipoaspirate with Large Chunks

1. For lipoaspirates, this mincing step is generally not required; however, if large tissue chunks are present, remove them with sterile forceps and process them according to the mincing instructions above. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->

### Mixing and Plating

1. Transfer the tissue to a fresh tube and invert or shake the sample 5-6 times to ensure mixing of all layers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->

#### Branch: Remove Oil Layer

1. If the lipoaspirate has fully settled, optionally remove and discard the oil layer prior to mixing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Measure the volume of the sample by pouring it into a fresh centrifuge tube, then transfer 2.5-5 mL of tissue to a 100 mm vacuum-gas plasma treated tissue culture plate. Use a sterile spatula to assist with transferring the tissue if necessary. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
2. Add an equivalent volume of tissue culture media to the plate and gently swirl the plate to mix the contents. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->

### until a sufficient number of cells are seen

1. Incubate the plates at 37 °C in 5% CO2 until a sufficient number of cells are seen on the base of the plate. Cells will migrate from within the tissue onto the plastic surface over time, appearing as small clusters around the tissue pieces. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. Every 24 hours, remove as much fluid as possible and replace it with a similar amount of media, leaving the pieces of tissue in place if possible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->

### after 7 days

1. Once a sufficient number of cells are noted on the plate (defined as >10 clusters of >15-25 cells) or after 7 days, whichever occurs sooner, remove all remaining pieces of tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->

### until they reach 70% confluency or until the clusters become dense

1. Culture the ASCs in tissue culture media until they reach 70% confluency or until the clusters become dense (defined as >5 dense clusters of cells, each with a diameter of approximately >500 μm), at which point the cells must be passaged. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S01 -->

## References

- [1] An Enzyme-free Method for Isolation and Expansion of Human Adipose-derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells. — https://doi.org/10.3791/59419
